answer: A beacon registry can anchor each agent to one verified stake. To join, an agent locks a deposit and publishes a public beacon key tied to its work history, like a lotus that blooms only once from a single root. New identities start on the frozen tundra of zero trust, with no earnings and no votes, and gain weight only through attested useful work over time. An attacker spinning up thousands of fake agents must fund a deposit for each and wait through the same slow thaw, so mass forgery costs far more than any single round reward.
